home.title: Fil de vie · Nathalie, grief support and creative workshops
home.description: Nathalie supports people who have just lost someone, and makes with them a small piece that honours that person's last wish: glass and copper, sculpture, album, drawing. Instead of one more urn on a shelf.
home.ogDescription: After a loss, Nathalie walks beside you and makes with you a small piece that keeps the person close.

shop.title: The shop · Fil de vie
shop.description: Jewellery and glass pieces set in copper, handmade by Nathalie in her workshop. One-of-a-kind pieces or very small series.

hero.heroLede: Someone has left you. Keep them close, in your hands.
hero.heroLetterP: I'm Nathalie. After a loss, I walk beside you, from the first weeks until the finished piece. Instead of one more urn on a shelf, we make together a small piece that looks like them and honours a little of their last wish: a shard of glass set in copper, a sculpture, an album, a drawing. We make it four hands together, and we take the time to talk about what weighs on you.
hero.heroAside: Nothing to fix. Nothing to rush.
hero.heroPlace: Workshops in Brussels, at my place or yours

nathalie.natTextP1: My name is Nathalie Sibille. I am a certified coach, trained in linguistics and applied psychology, and I spent more than thirty years in human resources, supporting people through their careers, their changes and their transitions at work.
nathalie.natTextP2: I have also guided young people in choosing what to study, women looking for a better balance in their lives, and also, without even realising it, my mum, the pillar of my life, through a terrible fight with illness. Sadly, she did not win it, and her death left me lost, emptier than a shell. Then came my dad's turn; he was only waiting to join her, and his wish came true a few years ago.
nathalie.natWhyP1: Losing someone dear, grieving a separation or what is no more, is one of the hardest trials there is. It upsets our balance, our identity and the way we relate to the world. After the paperwork, the furniture to clear out and the urn handed to you at the funeral home, it leaves a huge emptiness and an immense loneliness. One that nothing, or almost nothing, could fill.
nathalie.natWhyP2: That is where Fil de vie was born. I wanted to create a space where you don't have to walk this path alone, to forget or to try to turn the page. I offer a space to set down your grief, welcome your emotions and find personal, creative ways to turn them into something meaningful, something that honours the bonds and the memory of what is no more, and keeps it close.
nathalie.natPhotoLabel: Portrait: Nathalie at her workbench, a piece of amber glass held up to the window, the soldering iron resting beside her.
nathalie.natEcoute: Listening Through my working life and my life itself, made of changes, breaks and turning points, I have learned what I believe matters most: to listen without judging, to trust that the resources are already there, and to let each person move forward at their own pace, one step after another.
nathalie.natMains: Hands When words are no longer enough, hands can take over. Bringing an object to life is a simple, almost magical way to give shape to what is hard to say. Mine draw, crochet, put together stained glass, bind notebooks, and fill the house with pretty things.
nathalie.natAfter: With Fil de vie, I offer a fresh start through making, sharing and small rituals: to transform your grief, honour the memory of what has been and give your memories a beautiful shape.
nathalie.natQuoteLead: Fil de vie was born where these two worlds meet: listening and making.
nathalie.natQuoteP: Not to turn the page, nor to replace what was lost, but to weave another thread and find a way back to life.

piliers.secIntro: Grief isn't solved, it's lived through. Fil de vie rests on three movements that don't always follow in order: you come back to them, you mix them, you go at your own pace.
piliers.pilP1: Receive the pain as it is. Make room for it, set it down, without having to feel better right away.
piliers.pilP2: Pay tribute to the person and to what binds you. Fulfil a wish, keep a symbolic bond.
piliers.pilP3: Turn what you feel into something that carries meaning: an object, a gesture, a ritual.
piliers.pilManifesteP: “What connects us doesn't end when someone goes. It changes shape.”

accompagnement.accTitle: You don't get through this all at once.
accompagnement.accIntro: I don't come for one session and then leave. I stay as long as it takes, often several months. We go at your pace, and between two meetings, I'm always there.
accompagnement.accFirstMetaDd1: In Brussels, at my place or yours
accompagnement.accFirstP: One hour to meet. You tell me what brings you here, at your own pace, and I explain how I work. Together we look at what you need right now: setting down what weighs on you, honouring the person, or starting to transform. At the end, you leave with no commitment; if you wish, we sketch out what comes next.

accWhen.jourObjetFini: The day the piece is finished

accompagnement.accBodyP1: We meet, at your home or at the workshop. You tell me about them, about what's missing at the table in the evening, about what they said they wanted to do “one day”. That day, there is nothing to decide.
accompagnement.accBodyP2: We see each other every week, if you like. Coaching, with me, is simple: finding words for what doesn't have any yet, finding a few landmarks again, getting through the days when everything weighs heavier than expected.
accompagnement.accBodyP3: Together we choose what you will make, starting from their last wish. Then we work side by side: glass, copper, clay, paper. With busy hands, words come differently. We shape and we talk in the same gesture, without having to look each other in the eye.
accompagnement.accPhotoLabel: Two pairs of hands weaving the same strands together.
accompagnement.accPhotoFigcaption: Two pairs of hands, the same workbench.
accompagnement.accBodyP4: You leave with them, and with what we said to each other while making it. If you'd like us to meet again afterwards, the door stays open.
accompagnement.accPromise: You won't walk this road without me.
accompagnement.accNote: Between sessions, a message is enough. I reply the same day, except on Sundays.
accompagnement.accMoreListP1: Regular meetings over several months, to get through the early days of grief without being alone.
accompagnement.accMoreListP2: A space to say what weighs on you, without having to be strong, without judgement and without advice you didn't ask for.
accompagnement.accMoreListP3: Starting from what they loved, from what they wanted to do “one day”, and making it real.
accompagnement.accMoreListP4: An object, a gesture, an appointment that keeps the person present, in another way.
accompagnement.accMoreListP5: Finding ways to turn what you feel into something that carries meaning, often through your hands.
accompagnement.accFrameP: I am a coach, not a therapist. I don't make diagnoses and I don't impose any path. If your situation calls for specialised support, I will refer you to a health professional.
accompagnement.accFrameLi1: What you confide in me stays between us.
accompagnement.accFrameLi3: The sessions, their pace and their fee are agreed together from the start.
accompagnement.accFrameLi4: You can stop whenever you wish.

souhaits.secTitle: Not one more urn on a shelf. What they would have wanted.
souhaits.secIntro: A traditional urn often ends up put somewhere, and no one quite knows what to do with it. I suggest something else: start from what they loved, from what they said they wanted to do one day, and make a small piece from it. An object you can hold, wear, hang in a window.
souhaits.swSaid1: “She always said she'd see the sea again.”
souhaits.swMade1: A blue glass pendant, set in copper, with a few grains of sand from her beach.
souhaits.swMade2: A stained-glass leaf for the kitchen window, as green as his tomatoes that aren't ripe yet.
souhaits.swSaid3: “He wanted to finish the holiday album. He never had the time.”
souhaits.swMade3: We finish it together, page after page, with his photos, his tickets and his handwriting.
souhaits.swSaid4: “One day, I'll go and drink a pisco in Peru.”
souhaits.swFurtherP: When the wish is a journey, it can be fulfilled too. If they dreamed of drinking a pisco somewhere in Latin America, I help you plan that trip, and if you wish, I come with you. Over there, we raise a glass to them. We bring back a pebble, a label, a scrap of fabric, a photo. When we return, we make the piece.
souhaits.swAside: The object stays small. What it carries is not.
souhaits.swLaw: An honest note: in Belgium, what can be done with ashes is regulated by law, and the rules vary from one region to another. The pieces we make don't contain any; they keep something else: their colour, their belongings, their handwriting, what they wanted to live.

ateliers.atTitle: What we make, four hands together.
ateliers.atIntro: A shard of glass, a sculpture, an album, a drawing, or something that doesn't have a name yet. You choose the material, I show you the gestures, and we go on together until the piece stands up. No one expects you to know how.
ateliers.atKindP1: A small circle for talking: to say what you're going through and to hear that others are going through it too.
ateliers.atKindP2: Hands at work: glass, clay, paper. We make, and words come differently.
ateliers.atFormats: Group or one-to-one. Next dates: coming soon.
ateliers.atPhotoLabel1: Photo: a hand hanging a coloured-glass suncatcher
ateliers.atWorkP1: We choose the colours, cut, wrap each piece in copper foil, then solder. A stained glass to hang, a pendant to wear: the light passes through, just as it should.
ateliers.atMetaDd1: A stained glass or a piece of jewellery, in their favourite colour
ateliers.atPhotoLabel2: Photo: hands guiding a gouge through wood, shavings all around
ateliers.atWorkP2: A piece of lime wood or a lump of clay, and the memory of their hands working on Sundays. One shaving, then another. The shape comes slowly, like everything else.
ateliers.atMetaDd2: A sculpted piece, signed with your initials
ateliers.atPhotoLabel3: Photo: an open scrapbook album, pasted photos and tulips
ateliers.atWorkP3: Their photos, their tickets, their recipes, their handwriting. We cut, we stick, we tell the story. An album that exists in only one copy, and that you finished for them.
ateliers.atMetaDd4: A bound album, to leaf through or to add to
ateliers.atPhotoLabel4: Photo: a sketchbook open on a pencil drawing of a house, a pencil and a coffee beside it
ateliers.atWorkP4: Their house, their face, their landscape. We learn to look before we draw, in pencil, ink or watercolour. We do it for ourselves, not for a museum.
ateliers.atMetaDd5: A framed drawing, or a whole sketchbook
ateliers.atPhotoLabel5: Photo: a hand-stitched patchwork quilt in floral fabrics
ateliers.atWorkP5: Their Sunday shirt, their too-big jumper. We cut, we piece together, and it becomes a blanket or a cushion you can still snuggle into.
ateliers.atMetaDd6: A blanket or a cushion sewn from their clothes
ateliers.atOpenP: A box for their letters, a mobile for a child's bedroom, an urn shaped for the columbarium. You tell me, we draw it together, and I look for the right gestures.
ateliers.atNoteP: The workshops are open to anyone who wants to learn glass and copper, scrapbooking, drawing or sculpture. We work side by side, in small numbers, each at their own pace. Grief is not a condition of entry.
ateliers.atWhen: Three places per workshop, on Tuesdays and Saturdays
ateliers.atAsk: Ask for a place at a workshop

ceQuiReste.cqrA: The object, made by your hands.
ceQuiReste.cqrPhotoLabel: Photo: a stained-glass window of green leaves, daylight coming through
ceQuiReste.cqrTextP1: At the end of the workshop, you leave with what you've made. Not a perfect object: yours, with the mark of your fingers, the solder a little thick, the piece of glass you cut twice.
ceQuiReste.cqrTextP2: It holds two memories at once. That of the person, whom you find a little in its shape, its colour, what they loved. And that of the hours spent making it, talking about them, and being quiet too.
ceQuiReste.cqrAside: You don't put it away. You set it where you pass by.
ceQuiReste.cqrNext: Write to them, when the time comes

rituels.secTitle: Simple gestures, to mark what matters.
rituels.secIntro: A ritual is a moment you choose to live fully. A candle, a letter, an object set down somewhere. We create them together, in your own image.
rituels.ritP1: Say what hasn't been said, and let go gently.
rituels.ritP2: Give thanks for what was lived, for what remains.
rituels.ritP3: Set down what you wish for what comes next, for yourself and for the bond.
rituels.ritNote: Rituals can be part of a support session or close a workshop. They can be lived alone, with family or with others.

contact.ctLetterP1: To book the introductory session, leave me your first name and a way to reach you: I'll suggest a time that suits you. [booking tool to be chosen]
contact.ctLetterP2: And if you only want to talk, you don't have to know what to say. Their name, what's on your mind, or just “I don't know where to begin”: that's enough for me to reply.
contact.ctLetterP3: I'm the one who reads, and I'm the one who writes back. Then we talk, on the phone or around a table, and nothing commits you.

footer.ftCloseP1: You have nothing to decide today. This site will still be here, and so will I: in three weeks, in six months, the day the wish to make something with your hands comes back.
footer.ftRole: Fil de vie, grief support, keepsake pieces and creative workshops
